Method/Site masking

Repeat and paralog masking

Mask repetitive and duplicated regions of a reference so reads cannot map ambiguously.

When to use this method

Use when

  • The genome contains gene families, duplicated genes, or other repeats, as is common in fungi.
  • Variant calls cluster in regions with unusually high or uneven coverage.

Combine with

  • Mobile element masking: Add it for bacteria, whose horizontally transferred elements are not necessarily repeated in the reference.
  • Custom masking: Add your own BED file for species-specific regions that prediction tools do not find.

Operation

Site masking

Implementations

  • MUMmer (nucmer self-alignment)
  • RepeatMasker

Needs

Reference genome

Produces

Mask regions

Aligning the reference against itself reveals regions that occur more than once. Masking them prevents reads from duplicated genes being placed at the wrong copy, which would otherwise create false variant calls.

Used by protocols

Specified by

  • Bacterial phylogenomic surveillanceStep 2 (optional)
  • Fungal phylogenomic surveillanceStep 2 (optional)

Other methods for this operation

  • Custom maskingMask regions you define yourself in a BED file, such as genes known to be unreliable for your species.
  • Mobile element maskingMask prophages, insertion sequences, and other mobile elements in a bacterial reference.
